packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 20 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of work or author. I
opened only PROMPT.md and the six image files of this packet; no web, search,
catalogue or edition. No image processing was needed for this packet. (A directory listing of the
responses folder showed me other packets' response file names; none opened.)

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview, face A) and image-004 (overview, face B): one small
  horizontal strip, with a grey-scale/mm target (label "230417" on the target).
  By the mm scale the strip is roughly 75-80 mm wide and c. 25-30 mm high. A
  piece of white repair tissue projects from one short side; on face A it
  carries a pencil note, sideways, something like "1/1/2"(?) or "3/14"(?).
- image-002 = left half of face A, image-003 = right half of face A (they
  overlap in the middle: the words "da[.]", "epi..", "..endaz" repeat).
- image-005 = left half of face B, image-006 = right half of face B (overlap:
  "est ig'la", "suo inferiori", "hec", "dulcedo g° o(mn)is").
- Text is upright in all images. Small, rapid, heavily abbreviated cursive
  book hand in brown ink. Red paraph marks; red vertical strokes touching
  capitals; one red underline (face B L4) and a red horizontal rule near the
  foot of face A.
- Face A: a ruled vertical line at the right bounds the text; to its right a
  blank margin. On the left half the surface is skinned/abraded and nearly
  blank; at the far lower left a ruled vertical with small boxed marginal
  letters ("apl"(?) over a rule, "k"(?) below). Tentative: the readable text is
  the right-hand part of a column (or the inner column of two), with a
  marginal note or index letters at left.
- Face B: ruled vertical line at the left bounds the text; a second ruled
  vertical at the right end of the lines, then a gap, then a further vertical
  with a red paraph and a few letters ("c.."), i.e. the start of another column
  or a marginal note. Tentative: two columns, of which the left is preserved
  for c. 5 lines.
- No running title, no enlarged initial, no interlinear gloss seen (several
  superscript abbreviation letters are part of the main text).
- Tentative interpretation only: scholastic prose with argument markers
  ("Et ... dicitur", "g(?)°" = ergo?). No inference about work, author or date.

SELECTED SPANS
Everything legible on both faces (the strip only holds 5-8 short lines per face).
Unread: the abraded left half of face A; the bottom line of face B; the stub
of the second column/margin on face B.

FACE B - image-005 (left half) continued on image-006 (right half); one text
line runs across both tiles; the join is marked "|"
image-005 L1 | image-006 L1: medietas(?) e(st) q(u)alitas | [s(ed)?] e(st) ig'la(?) mi[..]:   (first word: "med'tas"/"mait'as" with a suspension stroke; top line, cropped above)
image-005 L2 | image-006 L2: d(icitu)r(?) : p(ro)p(ri)e(?) sup(er)ioris a'i(?) de | suo inferiori co(n)si(?)[..]
image-005 L3 | image-006 L3: nerit(?) co(n)(?). p(re)d(i)c(t)a [red-touched] Et g° d(icitu)r(?) | h(e)c(?) man[..]
image-005 L4 | image-006 L4: [..] valet(?) [superscript "al"(?)] de aliq(u)a(?) [struck or underlined in red] e(st) dulcedo g° | o(mn)is albedo   [red underline beneath "dulcedo g° o(mn)is albedo", continuing left under "de aliqua(?)"]
image-005 L5: e(st) dulcedo [tops of 3-4 abbreviation strokes only, rest lost in abrasion] | image-006 L5: [abbreviation strokes only, illegible]
image-005 L6 (foot, after a blank/abraded band): [..] ex(?) a[..] [illegible, cut]
image-006, right of the second vertical rule: "c[..]" then a red paraph; lower "p"(?) and a cross-like mark; faint grey offset letters at the far right edge, [illegible].
Notes: "g°" (g with superscript o) occurs three times; I give it unexpanded
because "ergo" vs. another resolution is not certain from the image. In L4
"omnis albedo est dulcedo" is how the letters fall across L4-L5
("o(mn)is albedo" end of L4, "e(st) dulcedo" start of L5); this is a reading
of visible letters, not a supplied sense.

FACE A - image-002 (left half) continued on image-003 (right half)
image-002 L1 | image-003 L1: [..]cto(?) [gap] [red vertical strokes] y[..]no(?) [..] | da[.] [..] a(n)ti(?)qua(?) cap(?)[..]   (top line, cropped above; last word ends in a looped abbreviation, "cap" + con/us-sign?)
image-002 L2 | image-003 L2: (et) s[..] [abraded] s(?) f(ac)te(?) ne. | [..]
   - the words of L1 and L2 are hard to separate at the left; on image-003 the first line reads: "da[.] [.]a a(n)ti(?)q(u)a(?) cap(?)"
image-002 L3 | image-003 L2: [a with stroke] [..] o(mn)ib(us)(?) / a(n)i(m)alib(us)(?) epi[..] | [..]b(us) falsio(?) ut
image-002 L4 | image-003 L3: [red-touched paraph] Et ad ista(m) [..] | [..]enda(m) dicu(n)t(?)   (above "dicu-" a small superscript "2"-shaped sign)
image-002 L5 | image-003 L4: co(?)[..]d(?)[blot] [abraded] | [three slanting hair-strokes above] o(mn)ib(us)(?) / o(mn)i(n)o(?)
image-003 L5: [red-touched paraph] Antiq(u)i(?) / A(n)te a(?) q(uod?)   (a diagonal pen stroke runs down from the last letter)
image-003 L6: [..]a m q(?) p(ro)ut(?)   (small superscript letters above; partly under a lifted strip)
image-003 L7: [..] a suis   [red horizontal rule below]
image-003 L8 (below the tear): [..] add[..]
image-002 foot, left of a ruled vertical: boxed marginal letters "apl"(?) [rule] "k"(?)
image-002 foot, right of that vertical (two short lines, torn):
   L-a: [illegible, abraded]
   L-b: m(?)° hoc d(icitu)r(?) n(on)(?) est ut k(?)[..]   (continuing into image-003 as "[..] a suis"? - alignment across the tear is uncertain)

LIMITATIONS
- A strip only; every line is cut at top/bottom context, and on face A the
  left half of each line is lost to abrasion, so no line is complete there.
- Which face is recto and which column is which cannot be determined.
- The cursive is heavily abbreviated; many expansions above are marked
  uncertain and several words are given only as letter shapes.
- Suggested further views: face A left half under raking or UV light; the
  adjacent strip(s) if this is one of several from the same binding.
